dek: Max Verstappen crushed Singapore for his second big win in a week as the title fight shifts.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix, leading every lap after fighting off Charles Leclerc at the start.

slides.label: The field
slides.text: Leclerc finished *second*, Kimi Antonelli third, and Lewis Hamilton a baffling sixth after a tyre gamble went wrong.

slides.label: The start
slides.text: Leclerc got the better launch but Verstappen *squeezed him toward the pit wall*, taking Turn One and never looking back.

slides.label: Ferrari chaos
slides.text: Hamilton stayed out on old soft tyres for *44 laps*, ignoring calls to pit, and got picked off late by three cars.

slides.label: The apology
slides.text: Hamilton admitted the call not to stop was his own and *apologized to Ferrari* right after the race.

slides.label: Title math
slides.text: Antonelli's podium plus George Russell's 9th-place finish stretch his championship lead to *102 points*.

slides.label: What's next
slides.text: At the US Grand Prix on October 25, 20-year-old Antonelli could become the *youngest F1 champion ever*.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: A 20-year-old rookie on the brink of history shows how fast the ladder can move when someone finally gets the seat.

cta_line: The gap is closing, one race at a *time*.
question: Does Antonelli clinch the title in Austin? Yes or no.
first_comment: Hamilton apologized to his own team on live TV after the strategy call backfired. That's how tight this race was.

caption_instagram:
Max Verstappen dominated the Singapore Grand Prix for his first win there, holding off Charles Leclerc at the start and controlling the race from front to back, according to BBC Sport.

It was Verstappen and Red Bull's second big win in a week after Malaysia. Meanwhile Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton stayed out on worn tyres for 44 laps against team advice, slid to sixth, and apologized to his team afterward. Mercedes rookie Kimi Antonelli took third, and with teammate George Russell finishing ninth, his championship lead jumped to 102 points heading into the US Grand Prix on October 25, where he could become the youngest F1 champion in history.

A 20-year-old this close to history is rare air in any sport.

Does Antonelli clinch the title in Austin? Yes or no.
